title: I spent months building a top-down action adventure with an AI-assisted workflow. The first 4 chapters are now a free demo on Steam.
author: WorldOFArtLover
selftext:
Temple Breaker is a top-down action adventure. You fight your way through a ruined temple, one chapter at a time: traps, puzzles, stealth sections and bosses. There are 15 chapters in the full game. The demo is the first 4, ending with the Broodmother boss.

I want to be upfront about how it was made, since that's what this sub is about:

* **Code:** I built it together with Codex. I designed the levels, mechanics and pacing, and Codex helped me build and debug them much faster than I could alone.
* **Art:** the environments, characters and key art were generated with GPT Image, then cleaned up, cut into sprites and fitted to the game by hand.
* **Testing:** every chapter was played through over and over on PC. AI can write a boss fight, but it can't tell you if the fight feels fair. That part was all trial and error.

What I learned:

1. AI is great at getting a mechanic working on day one. Making it *feel* good still takes days of tuning.
2. Keeping the art style consistent across 15 chapters was harder than any code problem.
3. Small, focused levels worked much better than asking for big systems in one go.

I built this alone, one chapter at a time. If you play the demo, please tell me what you think, even if it's harsh. What worked, what felt off, where you quit. Every comment helps me make the full game better. ❤️

Steam link is in the comments.
